concepts.why: Biblical-theological / secular scholar: Daniel 7:1 says a dream and visions passed through his mind in bed; it does not say the heavens opened. Isaiah 6:1 and Zechariah 1:8 were dropped in round one for the same reason (they say 'I saw'). Four passages remain (Ezekiel 1:1, Revelation 4:1, 19:11, Acts 7:56).

Secular scholar / biblical-theological: Revelation 3:8 is an open door that no one can shut, with no key in it. The concept is named for keys, and 3:7 already carries 'what He opens no one can shut'. Five passages remain.

concepts.name: How long, O Lord? and the blood of His servants avenged
concepts.why: Secular scholar / biblical-theological: 'How long' is said only in Psalm 79:5, Habakkuk 1:2, Zechariah 1:12, Daniel 8:13 and Revelation 6:10. Psalm 79:10, Deuteronomy 32:43 and Revelation 19:2 are about blood avenged and do not say 'how long', so the old name (the table row's second half) covers only part of the passages. The compound name is a plain label and fits all eight; the Revelation 6:10 to 19:2 link is the text's own.

concepts.name: The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish reader of the Hebrew Bible: 'moon to blood' is said only in Joel 2:31, Acts 2:20 and Revelation 6:12; Isaiah 13:10, Joel 2:10, Matthew 24:29, Isaiah 34:4 and Revelation 6:13-14 say darkened sun, dimmed moon and falling stars or a rolled-up sky. Isaiah 13:10 and Matthew 24:29 give the common wording, which every passage holds (Joel 2:31 and Acts 2:20 say 'turned to darkness'). The notes stay as they are.

concepts.name: He lifted up his hand to heaven
concepts.why: Secular scholar / biblical-theological: only Daniel 12:7 and Revelation 10:6 say he swore by Him who lives forever. Genesis 14:22 has Abram raising his hand to the LORD (no oath by another), and Deuteronomy 32:40 has God Himself lifting His hand and swearing by His own life. What all four hold is the raised hand: Revelation 10:5 'lifted up his right hand to heaven', Daniel 12:7 'raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven', Deuteronomy 32:40 'I lift up My hand to heaven', Genesis 14:22 'I have raised my hand to the LORD'. The oath words stay in the notes of Daniel 12:7 and Revelation 10:5-6.

concepts.name: A kingdom that will never be destroyed
concepts.why: Baptist/dispensational, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers: 'They will receive the kingdom' puts one 'they' over Daniel's saints of the Most High (7:18, 7:27), Luke 12:32's little flock and Revelation 5:10's 'them', which is the Israel-and-church question again; and Daniel 2:44 (God sets up a kingdom) and Revelation 11:15 (the kingdom of the world has become the Lord's) do not say anyone receives it. 'A kingdom that will never be destroyed' is Daniel 2:44 and 7:14's own wording, fits all seven passages, and leaves who receives it to the notes.

concepts.name: Their fire will never be quenched
concepts.why: Secular scholar / biblical-theological: the worm is in Isaiah 66:24 and Mark 9:48 only. Isaiah 1:31, Ezekiel 20:48 and Matthew 3:12 say only that the fire is not quenched, so the name says more than three of the five passages. Isaiah 66:24's own phrase 'their fire will never be quenched' holds all five, and the worm stays in the two notes that have it.

Baptist/dispensational and Reformed readers (the order of the last things): Psalm 90:4 and 2 Peter 3:8 do not speak of Revelation 20's thousand years and neither cites the other; they are the passages one school of reading sets beside Revelation 20 to say the years are not literal. Putting them in one concept with Revelation 20:2-7 takes that side by grouping, whatever the notes say. Revelation 20:2-3, 20:4, 20:5-6 and 20:7 remain (four passages), and the concept says only what Revelation says.

concepts.name: The bride, the wife of the Lamb
concepts.why: Baptist/dispensational, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers (Israel and the church): 'The new Jerusalem, prepared as a bride' says the bride is the city across all seven passages, but only Revelation 21:2 and 21:9-10 say so; Revelation 19:7, 19:9 and 22:17 speak of the bride and the marriage without naming Jerusalem, and readers part on whether the bride of 19:7 and 22:17 is the city. 'The bride, the wife of the Lamb' (Revelation 21:9) is the texts' own word, fits every passage, and leaves the 21:2 note to say the city is prepared as a bride, with concept 69 holding the city.

subtitle_and_order.finding: The subtitle says the concepts 'follow the order of the books, chiefly Revelation's'. That is true only at the level of Revelation's chapter blocks (1-3, 4-5, 6-7, 8-11, 12-14, 15-18, 20, 21-22). Inside blocks and at the edges it is not: the first eight concepts are the seers' experience of being shown (opened heaven, Spirit, mystery, angel, question, interpretation, falling facedown, host), with concepts 5 (Rev 7:13) and 8 (Rev 5:11) among Revelation 1 material; 28-32 follow Matthew 24 and Malachi, not Revelation; 49-51 are Daniel set amid Revelation 12-14; and several pairs run against Revelation's verse order. A reader who tests the subtitle will find these.

33 (Day of the LORD, Rev 6:17) and 34 (hiding among the rocks, Rev 6:15): 34 should come first

subtitle_and_order.suggested_subtitle: What the seers were shown, in the texts' own words; the concepts run in blocks, from Revelation's first chapters to its last, and are not an order of events
subtitle_and_order.why: Either reorder the six pairs and keep 'order of the books', or use the softer subtitle, which says what is true. As to sides on the last things: ordering by Revelation's chapters is not a claim about events, and the Matthew 24 run (28-30) is Matthew's own order, so no reader should take it for a timeline. The sequence 61 thousand years, 62 thrones, 64 books, 63 resurrection, 65 second death, 66 new heaven follows Revelation 20-21 and is Revelation's order, not an assertion.

duplicates.why: Both are fire that does not end: 54 'Fire and sulfur, and smoke that rises forever' already holds Isaiah 34:10 ('It will not be quenched ... Its smoke will ascend forever'), the same image as 55's 'fire will never be quenched'. They differ only in vocabulary (sulfur and smoke against worm and unquenched flame). If the owner wants one node for the unending fire, fold 55's five passages into 54; if two, keep both, since the owner has said overlap is welcome.

secondary_or_links: Links: add Sin/Exile/Death back now the ten-link cap is lifted. The grounds are concepts 63 (the dead who awake, Daniel 12:2, Revelation 20:13), 65 (the second death) and 17 (the keys of Death and Hades, Revelation 1:18).
Secondary concepts: 'A time, times, and half a time' should be promoted or widened (see missing); at present it holds three passages and leaves out the texts' other counts of the same period.
Secondary concepts: no other change. Ten secondary concepts is at the limit; adding anything means dropping one.

Concept 61 after the change has Revelation 20 only; if the owner prefers the concept to stay two-book, it can be re-seated as a secondary concept pairing nothing, but a one-book concept is allowed since 65 'The second death' is also Revelation-only.
About view and numbers: no check made here; nothing in this review changes what is extracted.

missing.sub_theme: Forty-two months, 1,260 days, a time, times, and half a time
missing.why: One period named in five different ways, developed across Daniel and Revelation (Daniel 12:7, Revelation 12:14 use the same words; Revelation 11:2-3, 12:6 and 13:5 give it in months and days). It is plainly and widely developed, is one of the best-known links between the two books, and is presently only a three-passage secondary concept. Listed in the texts' words only; no claim about what the period is, when it falls, or whether the counts are the same period.
